title: Jaishankar calls attacks on shipping 'simply unacceptable' as India hosts Indian Ocean ministers
dek: Opening the first IORA ministerial under India's chairship, the minister urged respect for the law of the sea as Gulf attacks on tankers and refineries continue.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said on Friday that attacks on merchant shipping and seafarers were "simply unacceptable" and called for a collective response, as he opened a meeting of foreign ministers and officials from the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) in New Delhi, the first under India's chairship of the group.

His remarks came as tankers and oil facilities in the Gulf came under repeated attack this week. Mr Jaishankar told the 25th IORA Council of Ministers that "international law, especially the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), must be respected", according to reports, and urged members to cooperate against terrorism, drug trafficking and illegal fishing.

## What he said

Speaking at the general debate, held under the theme "A Stronger Regional Voice: Positioning IORA in a Changing Global Order", Mr Jaishankar described a world of conflicts, frictions and disruptions but said it was "equally imperative to appreciate the promising aspects" of a changing order, including "deep interdependence, strong globalisation and the benefits of international cooperation", according to reports. "We have to become more self-reliant as well as more enthusiastic about cooperating with partners," he said.

"The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity and economic prosperity," he said in his opening remarks. "It is our collective responsibility to ensure that this region remains peaceful, stable and secure." He said the ministers' deliberations would "provide clear direction for the future of IORA".

He said India's approach to the group was guided by its MAHASAGAR policy, short for "Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions", which builds on the earlier SAGAR doctrine for the Indian Ocean. India's priorities as chair include deeper engagement with dialogue partners, practical regional projects and a stronger financial and institutional base for the association, according to reports. He thanked Sri Lanka for its term as the previous chair and welcomed Mauritius as vice-chair and the next chair. No joint statement or decisions from the meeting had been reported by Friday evening.

## Why it matters

IORA brings together 23 countries around the Indian Ocean, from Australia, Indonesia and Singapore to South Africa, Kenya and the Gulf. Its members include Iran and Yemen, as well as Oman and the UAE, which sit on either side of the Strait of Hormuz, and Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and the Maldives in India's neighbourhood. Its 12 dialogue partners include the United States, China, Russia, the European Union and Saudi Arabia. That puts several parties to the conflicts now disrupting Gulf shipping in the same forum.

For India, the sea routes through the Gulf and the Red Sea carry most of its oil imports and much of its trade with Europe and West Asia. Reports have linked Mr Jaishankar's remarks to wider concern over attacks on merchant ships in West Asia and the Black Sea in which Indian sailors have been killed. Many of the world's merchant seafarers are Indian, so attacks on ships often put Indian crew at risk.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre has recorded dozens of attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz since October, and this week a projectile hit Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast, killing a Nepali worker. The Indian Ocean is also an arena of growing competition between India and China, whose navy and research vessels have stepped up their presence in the region and whose state companies have financed ports in Sri Lanka, Myanmar and elsewhere.

## Background

IORA was set up in 1997 to promote economic cooperation among Indian Ocean states; its secretariat is in Mauritius. India took over the rotating chair from Sri Lanka for 2025 to 2027 under the theme "Innovation, Openness, Resilience and Adaptability in the Indian Ocean Region". A meeting of the group's senior officials was held in New Delhi on 25 and 26 November before the ministers met.
